author: reek
body: The counts are pinned by multiplying them back to the total, which is the same check the extractor makes against the oracle. A count wrong in one length and compensating in another still fails a word read at a known offset.

author: reek
body: The four words, as the bytes a decoder would copy: "time", "down", """, and the opening of a script tag.

author: reek
body: The index finds a word where one is and does not find one where none is. "xx" in front and "yy" behind put the word off the start of the input, because a matcher that only ever looks at position zero passes a test built at position zero.

author: reek
body: The negative case is the half that matters. A lookup that answered a slot for every position would pass every positive case here and corrupt every stream.
